description:
About the Position

Umea University advertises a fully funded four-year PhD student position in statistics, focused on next-generation latent variable models. Latent variable models - factor models, item-response models, mixed models and their modern extensions - are central to statistics, psychometrics and data science, and the project develops methodology that improves how such models handle high-dimensional, heterogeneous and dependent data. The doctoral candidate will work on theory, computation and applications, publishing in international statistics journals.

Umea's statistics environment offers strong computational training and connections to applied fields across the university's faculties, and the position is a salaried four-year employment under the Swedish collective agreement with full social benefits. Doctoral researchers in Sweden are employed members of staff, and Umea's graduate school in science provides coursework, travel funding and an international seminar programme to support the candidate's development.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in statistics, mathematics, econometrics or a closely related quantitative field, with strong foundations in probability and inference and demonstrable programming ability. Interest in computational statistics or machine learning connections is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Umea University's Varbi portal with CV, transcripts, references and a statement of research interests; the closing date is 4 November 2026.

Highlights

  • Fully funded 4-year PhD in statistics at Umea University
  • Next-generation latent variable model methodology
  • Theory, computation and applied collaborations
  • Salaried employment under the Swedish collective agreement
  • Graduate-school training and travel funding
  • Closing date: 4 November 2026
